result.summary: The intersection is controlled by vehicle traffic signals but lacks any marked crosswalks or pedestrian signal heads. Pedestrians must navigate a two-lane roadway with sight lines partially obstructed by parked vehicles near the corners.

hazards.name: Unmarked Crosswalks
hazards.description: The absence of painted crosswalks at a signalized intersection fails to define a clear path for pedestrians or alert drivers to their presence.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Signals
hazards.description: No pedestrian-specific signal heads are visible, leaving pedestrians to rely on vehicle signals which may not provide adequate clearance time.

hazards.name: Sight Line Obstructions
hazards.description: Vehicles parked close to the intersection corners obstruct the view between pedestrians waiting to cross and approaching motorists.
hazards.location_in_image: Left and right curbsides near the intersection

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk Markings
interventions.description: Install continental-style crosswalk markings on all legs of the intersection to clearly define pedestrian space.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Signal Heads
interventions.description: Install pedestrian countdown signals to provide clear timing information for people crossing the street.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Construct curb extensions to reduce the crossing distance and improve visibility by moving pedestrians past the line of parked cars.

result.summary: The intersection features basic pedestrian infrastructure including sidewalks and a traffic signal, but lacks modern safety enhancements. Faded crosswalk markings and the absence of dedicated pedestrian signals increase risk for people crossing the street in this mixed-use urban environment.

hazards.name: Faded Crosswalks
hazards.description: The painted crosswalk markings across the side street are significantly worn, reducing their visibility to approaching motorists.
hazards.location_in_image: Across the intersection of Ontario St.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Signals
hazards.description: No dedicated pedestrian signal heads are visible at this signalized intersection, forcing pedestrians to rely on vehicle signals.
hazards.location_in_image: At the traffic light pole on the corner.

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions from Parking
hazards.description: Vehicles parked close to the intersection corners may block sightlines between pedestrians and drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curbs of both streets near the intersection corners.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Repaint the crosswalks using a continental or ladder pattern to increase visibility for drivers.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Signal Installation
interventions.description: Install pedestrian countdown signals to provide clear information on when it is safe to cross.

interventions.title: Intersection Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces within 20 feet of the intersection to improve sightlines for all road users.

result.summary: The intersection is equipped with vehicular traffic signals and sidewalks but lacks basic pedestrian safety infrastructure such as marked crosswalks and dedicated pedestrian signals. The wide, unmarked roadway and presence of parked vehicles near the corner create a environment where pedestrians are exposed and less visible to drivers.

hazards.name: Unmarked Crossing
hazards.description: Despite being a signalized intersection, there are no painted crosswalks to designate pedestrian right-of-way.

hazards.name: Missing Pedestrian Signals
hazards.description: No pedestrian-specific signal heads are visible, which can lead to confusion regarding when it is safe to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Traffic signal poles at the intersection

hazards.name: Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along the curb near the intersection may block the view between drivers and pedestrians waiting to cross.

result.summary: The environment is a typical urban mixed-use street with narrow sidewalks but a complete lack of marked pedestrian crossing infrastructure. Pedestrians must cross an unmarked intersection with potential sightline obstructions from parked vehicles and no dedicated traffic control for the primary roadway.
